embedded-closure.claim_text: ML modules can approximate poorly characterised regulatory or kinetic processes inside an otherwise mechanistic framework, raising predictive accuracy without requiring fully resolved mechanisms.

candidates.paper_title: Sparse and Compositionally Robust Inference of Microbial Ecological Networks

useful_outcomes.rationale: SPIEC-EASI infers OTU networks via inverse covariance; not a closure model embedded in a mechanistic framework.

immediate_benefit.rationale: Open R/Python tool exists, but it learns associations rather than closing kinetic gaps in a WCM.

plausible.rationale: Sound graphical-model methodology with cross-validation, but the link to closure-style hybrid modelling is indirect.

scalable.rationale: Demonstrated on hundreds of OTUs; nothing about whole-cell-scale kinetic processes.

how_to_validate.rationale: Stability selection and synthetic benchmarks help, but they target network inference not embedded ML closure.

candidates.paper_title: Deep learning for universal linear embeddings of nonlinear dynamics

useful_outcomes.rationale: Learned Koopman embedding linearises nonlinear dynamics, indirectly demonstrating ML closure of unknown dynamical structure.

immediate_benefit.rationale: Auto-encoder architecture is reproducible, but adapting to mechanistic biological submodels still requires substantial work.

plausible.rationale: Method connects to Koopman theory and shows compact eigenfunction representations on benchmark systems.

scalable.rationale: Examples are low-dimensional dynamical systems, far from 10^5-variable cell-scale problems.

how_to_validate.rationale: Validated against analytical Koopman spectra and reconstruction error on known systems.

candidates.paper_title: Structural Properties of the Caenorhabditis elegans Neuronal Network

useful_outcomes.rationale: Paper analyses C. elegans wiring topology; no ML closure of mechanistic gaps is presented.

immediate_benefit.rationale: Wiring data is reusable but offers no embedded ML method for WCM closure.

plausible.rationale: Network statistics are sound but not relevant to ML-mechanistic hybrid closure claim.

scalable.rationale: Single small connectome; not addressing whole-cell scale mechanistic processes.

how_to_validate.rationale: Topology consistency checks are not a transferable validation strategy for hybrid closure.

candidates.paper_title: Chaos as an intermittently forced linear system

useful_outcomes.rationale: HAVOK closes nonlinear chaos by data-driven forcing on top of a linear Koopman model — closure analogue.

immediate_benefit.rationale: Delay-embedding + SVD pipeline is straightforward, but applying to biological kinetics needs adaptation.

plausible.rationale: Validated on Lorenz, magnetic-field reversals and measles outbreaks with consistent forcing statistics.

scalable.rationale: Demonstrated on low-dimensional time series; whole-cell scale untested.

how_to_validate.rationale: Compares forcing-statistics signatures across canonical and real systems, a borrowable ablation pattern.

candidates.paper_title: DPM: A deep learning PDE augmentation method with application to large-eddy simulation

useful_outcomes.rationale: Title and venue indicate a deep PDE-augmentation closure for LES, directly exemplifying ML closure of unresolved subgrid physics.

immediate_benefit.rationale: LES code-coupled deep models are achievable, though biological PDE coupling adds plumbing.

plausible.rationale: Published in JCP; LES-with-NN closure is a well-supported methodology in the field.

scalable.rationale: LES is a multimillion-DOF problem, supporting scalability claims even though biology specifics differ.

how_to_validate.rationale: DPM-style works typically validate against high-fidelity DNS, a transferable gold-standard pattern.

candidates.paper_title: Data-driven closures for stochastic dynamical systems

useful_outcomes.rationale: Title explicitly addresses data-driven closure of stochastic dynamical systems — closely matching the closure claim.

immediate_benefit.rationale: Methodology likely exists in code form, but bridging stochastic chemistry submodels still demands engineering.

plausible.rationale: JCP venue and topic suggest sound methodology, though abstract is missing for deeper assessment.

scalable.rationale: Without abstract details, scalability to 10^5 variables is uncertain; stochastic systems are typically modest-sized.

how_to_validate.rationale: Closure papers typically include ablation against full stochastic ground truth, a useful template.

candidates.paper_title: Symplectic Model Reduction of Hamiltonian Systems on Nonlinear Manifolds and Approximation with Weakly Symplectic Autoencoder

useful_outcomes.rationale: Symplectic-manifold ROM preserves structure but is reduction, not closure of poorly characterised kinetics.

immediate_benefit.rationale: Hamiltonian framework rarely matches dissipative biological networks; non-trivial port to WCM.

plausible.rationale: Mathematically rigorous: introduces symplectic manifold Galerkin with explicit structure-preservation guarantees.

scalable.rationale: Designed for high-dimensional Hamiltonian PDEs but not demonstrated at whole-cell scale.

how_to_validate.rationale: Energy-conservation and stability benchmarks are valuable validation checks for any reduced model.

candidates.paper_title: Comparison of neural closure models for discretised PDEs

useful_outcomes.rationale: Systematically compares derivative-fitting and trajectory-fitting neural closures on Burgers and Kuramoto-Sivashinsky.

immediate_benefit.rationale: Provides clear training-loss prescriptions (trajectory + discretise-then-optimise) directly reusable for closure models.

plausible.rationale: Findings backed by accuracy/stability comparisons across two benchmark PDEs and three loss procedures.

scalable.rationale: Tested on small 1D PDEs; cell-scale dimensionality unaddressed.

how_to_validate.rationale: Explicitly contrasts derivative versus trajectory fitting, an ablation pattern WCM teams can adopt.

candidates.paper_title: Curvature effects in turbulent premixed flames of H2/Air: a DNS study with reduced chemistry

useful_outcomes.rationale: DNS study with reduced chemistry but no embedded ML closure module.

immediate_benefit.rationale: Combustion chemistry reduction is hand-engineered; no ML pipeline to lift directly into WCM.

plausible.rationale: Standard DNS analysis is sound, but the closure-claim relevance is tangential.

scalable.rationale: DNS is high-DOF but the reduced chemistry mechanism is small and not learned.

how_to_validate.rationale: PDF analysis of OH radical states is a niche validation tool, not transferable to ML closure.

candidates.paper_title: Exploring the beta distribution in variable-density turbulent mixing

useful_outcomes.rationale: Assumed-PDF closure for turbulent mixing, but uses statistical (beta) closure rather than ML.

immediate_benefit.rationale: Stochastic-differential-equation derivation is mathematics-heavy and not a plug-in ML closure.

plausible.rationale: Mathematically grounded extension of beta-PDF closure to variable-density mixing.

scalable.rationale: Closure approach is generic but not demonstrated at WCM scale or with ML acceleration.

how_to_validate.rationale: Comparison of moment equations to mass conservation is narrow and not ML-specific.

embedded-constraint.claim_text: Mechanistic priors regularise or structure ML predictions so that learned components remain biologically plausible and generalise outside the training distribution.

candidates.paper_title: Physics-informed neural networks: A deep learning framework for solving forward and inverse problems involving nonlinear partial differential equations

useful_outcomes.rationale: Foundational PINN paper showing PDE residual penalties keep NN predictions consistent with physics across forward/inverse tasks.

immediate_benefit.rationale: Mature open-source frameworks (DeepXDE, JAX) wrap this method; adoption costs are low for ODE/PDE-style biology.

plausible.rationale: Extensively validated on canonical PDEs (Burgers, Schrodinger) with low residuals and 15k+ citations.

scalable.rationale: Scales to moderate PDE problems but vanilla PINNs struggle with stiff multi-timescale systems typical of WCMs.

how_to_validate.rationale: Provides residual-based loss diagnostics and synthetic-data ablations, a directly borrowable validation template.

candidates.paper_title: Physics-informed machine learning

useful_outcomes.rationale: Reviews concrete physics-prior wins (PINN, operator learning) where mechanistic constraints improve generalisation.

immediate_benefit.rationale: Acts as a curated pointer to mature methods and code; reduces decision overhead for WCM teams.

plausible.rationale: Authoritative Nature Reviews synthesis with broad evidence base from scientific ML community.

scalable.rationale: Surveys methods at varying scales but does not itself demonstrate cell-scale deployment.

how_to_validate.rationale: Discusses validation idioms (ablation, generalisation tests) but at survey level rather than recipe level.

candidates.paper_title: Understanding and Mitigating Gradient Flow Pathologies in Physics-Informed Neural Networks

useful_outcomes.rationale: Diagnoses and fixes gradient pathologies in PINNs, indirectly improving how mechanistic priors regularise training.

immediate_benefit.rationale: Provides adaptive loss-balancing tricks reusable in any PINN-style WCM closure or constraint module.

plausible.rationale: SIAM SISC paper with formal stiff-dynamics analysis backing the mitigation strategies.

scalable.rationale: Helps PINNs handle stiff problems, partially relevant to multi-timescale cell models.

how_to_validate.rationale: Demonstrates failure modes via loss-landscape diagnostics, a useful PINN validation pattern.

candidates.paper_title: Physics-informed neural networks for high-speed flows
candidates.paper_journal: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering

useful_outcomes.rationale: Applies PINN constraints (Euler equations) to compressible flow, demonstrating prior-driven generalisation.

immediate_benefit.rationale: Code patterns transfer to PDE-style biology, but high-speed-flow specifics are domain-distant from WCM.

plausible.rationale: Peer-reviewed CMAME paper with 1k+ citations applying PINNs to a hard physics regime.

scalable.rationale: Handles shocks via tailored loss; moderate scalability but not WCM-scale demonstrated.

how_to_validate.rationale: Compares against numerical solvers and exact solutions, an adoptable gold-standard ablation.

candidates.paper_title: NSFnets (Navier-Stokes flow nets): Physics-informed neural networks for the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations

useful_outcomes.rationale: Embeds incompressible NS constraints into NN solver, showing physics priors improve flow predictions.

immediate_benefit.rationale: NSFnets recipe is reusable, but mapping to reaction-diffusion biology takes engineering.

plausible.rationale: Strong validation against DNS for canonical NS benchmarks, supporting the methodology.

scalable.rationale: Demonstrates NS solver at moderate Reynolds; 10^5 DOF cell-scale not addressed.

how_to_validate.rationale: DNS comparison and divergence-free residuals offer a transferable validation template.

candidates.paper_title: A physics-informed deep learning framework for inversion and surrogate modeling in solid mechanics
candidates.paper_journal: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering

useful_outcomes.rationale: Solid-mechanics PINN handles inversion under physics constraints, supporting prior-regularised ML.

immediate_benefit.rationale: Framework is general but solid-mechanics governing equations differ from biochemistry, requiring adaptation.

plausible.rationale: 1k+ citations and CMAME peer review back the inversion and surrogate-modelling methodology.

scalable.rationale: Inversion problems shown at moderate mesh sizes; whole-cell scale untested.

how_to_validate.rationale: Benchmarks against FEM solutions provide a borrowable gold-standard validation pattern.

candidates.paper_title: When and why PINNs fail to train: A neural tangent kernel perspective

useful_outcomes.rationale: Identifies NTK-based failure regimes for physics-constrained NNs, indirectly improving prior-regularised training.

immediate_benefit.rationale: Provides loss-weighting prescriptions that drop into existing PINN-style hybrid pipelines.

plausible.rationale: Backed by neural tangent kernel theory and JCP-quality empirical analysis with 1k+ citations.

scalable.rationale: NTK insights help stiff regimes seen in larger PINN problems but cell-scale unproven.

how_to_validate.rationale: Failure-mode characterisation provides a diagnostic protocol for new constrained ML applications.

candidates.paper_title: Conservative physics-informed neural networks on discrete domains for conservation laws: Applications to forward and inverse problems
candidates.paper_journal: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering

useful_outcomes.rationale: Conservative PINN enforces conservation-law constraints, directly making ML predictions physically plausible.

immediate_benefit.rationale: Conservation-form constraints map naturally onto stoichiometric and mass-balance constraints in WCM contexts.

plausible.rationale: 1k+ citation CMAME paper with peer-reviewed forward and inverse benchmarks.

scalable.rationale: Discrete-domain decomposition supports moderate scaling; full-cell scale not yet demonstrated.

how_to_validate.rationale: Direct comparison with conservation residuals and inverse-problem ground truth — borrowable validation.

candidates.paper_title: B-PINNs: Bayesian physics-informed neural networks for forward and inverse PDE problems with noisy data

useful_outcomes.rationale: Bayesian PINN combines mechanistic PDE priors with uncertainty quantification, regularising ML predictions under noisy data.

immediate_benefit.rationale: Bayesian inference on top of PINN adds compute cost and tooling overhead for WCM teams.

plausible.rationale: JCP-quality methodology with formal posterior sampling and noise-robust benchmarks.

scalable.rationale: Bayesian sampling further limits scale; whole-cell-size deployment is unrealistic without surrogates.

how_to_validate.rationale: Posterior-based calibration and noise-injection ablations are an excellent template for hybrid model UQ.

candidates.paper_title: Physics-constrained deep learning for high-dimensional surrogate modeling and uncertainty quantification without labeled data

useful_outcomes.rationale: Physics-constrained NN trains without labels, leveraging mechanistic priors to keep predictions plausible — direct match.

immediate_benefit.rationale: Label-free training is attractive when WCM ground truth is scarce; methodology is reproducible.

plausible.rationale: JCP paper with 1k+ citations applying physics-constrained learning to high-dimensional surrogates.

scalable.rationale: Explicitly targets high-dimensional surrogate modelling, partially supporting WCM-scale ambitions.

how_to_validate.rationale: Provides UQ comparisons and constraint-satisfaction checks usable as validation patterns.

embedded-emulation.claim_text: ML surrogates can replace expensive mechanistic submodules — such as spatial dynamics, stochastic chemistry, or molecular simulations — to make whole-cell-scale simulation tractable on accessible hardware.

candidates.paper_title: Learning nonlinear operators via DeepONet based on the universal approximation theorem of operators

useful_outcomes.rationale: DeepONet learns operator maps replacing PDE solvers — canonical surrogate for expensive mechanistic submodules.

immediate_benefit.rationale: Open DeepONet code and clear training recipe make adoption straightforward for biological PDE/ODE submodules.

plausible.rationale: Backed by universal approximation theorem and 2.6k citations across operator-learning applications.

scalable.rationale: Operator nets scale across discretisations and have been pushed toward large-scale physics emulation.

how_to_validate.rationale: Compares against numerical solvers across diverse PDE benchmarks — directly transferable validation template.

candidates.paper_title: Climate policy implications of nonlinear decline of Arctic land permafrost and other cryosphere elements

useful_outcomes.rationale: PAGE-ICE integrates dynamic emulators of complex physical models — concrete surrogate-replacement example, but climate not biology.

immediate_benefit.rationale: Methodology is climate-economic; transferring emulators to WCM submodules requires fresh training.

plausible.rationale: Nature Communications publication with quantitative downstream policy effects supports the emulator approach.

scalable.rationale: Shows emulators replacing expensive Earth-system models, demonstrating the surrogate concept at scale.

how_to_validate.rationale: Validates by comparing economic impact under multiple Paris-aligned scenarios — domain-specific ablation.

candidates.paper_title: Learning the solution operator of parametric partial differential equations with physics-informed DeepONets

useful_outcomes.rationale: Physics-informed DeepONets predict PDE solutions up to three orders of magnitude faster than conventional solvers.

immediate_benefit.rationale: Combines surrogate speed with physics priors and trains without paired data — high payoff for WCM submodule replacement.

plausible.rationale: Science Advances publication with quantitative speedups across multiple parametric PDE families.

scalable.rationale: Operator-learning architecture scales across parameter regimes and discretisations.

how_to_validate.rationale: Speedup-versus-solver and parameter-sweep ablations are a directly adoptable validation strategy.

candidates.paper_title: Neural operators for accelerating scientific simulations and design

useful_outcomes.rationale: Reviews concrete neural-operator surrogate wins in fluids, materials, and biology, directly supporting emulation claim.

immediate_benefit.rationale: Survey points at multiple usable architectures but offers no single drop-in tool.

plausible.rationale: Nature Reviews Physics synthesis grounded in dozens of validated applications.

scalable.rationale: Emphasises operator learning as the path to scalable scientific surrogates across disciplines.

how_to_validate.rationale: Discusses validation idioms across operator-learning case studies but at survey granularity.

candidates.paper_title: MIONet: Learning Multiple-Input Operators via Tensor Product

useful_outcomes.rationale: MIONet extends operator learning to multiple-input operators, broadening the class of mechanistic submodules emulable.

immediate_benefit.rationale: Reference implementation exists; multi-input formulation matches biology where states + parameters + signals co-vary.

plausible.rationale: Provides universal approximation theorem for multiple-input operators plus error analysis and ODE/PDE benchmarks.

scalable.rationale: Demonstrated on canonical ODE/PDE systems — extension to whole-cell scale not yet shown.

how_to_validate.rationale: Approximation-error bounds plus benchmarks against ODE/PDE solutions provide a borrowable validation pattern.

candidates.paper_title: Wavelet Neural Operator for solving parametric partial differential equations in computational mechanics problems
candidates.paper_journal: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering

useful_outcomes.rationale: Wavelet neural operator emulates parametric PDE solvers in mechanics — concrete surrogate example, slightly distant from biology.

immediate_benefit.rationale: Standard neural-operator code patterns apply; wavelet basis adds modest complexity.

plausible.rationale: CMAME paper with 150+ citations and benchmark studies on parametric PDEs.

scalable.rationale: Multiscale wavelet basis aids resolution scaling but cell-scale dimensionality is unproven.

how_to_validate.rationale: Compares against finite-element solutions across multiple PDEs — adoptable gold-standard test.

candidates.paper_title: A comprehensive and FAIR comparison between MLP and KAN representations for differential equations and operator networks
candidates.paper_journal: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering

useful_outcomes.rationale: Benchmarks MLP vs KAN inside operator networks, informing best surrogate architectures for emulation.

immediate_benefit.rationale: Architecture-comparison findings directly guide WCM-team choice between MLP and KAN backbones.

plausible.rationale: FAIR comparison protocol on standard benchmarks lends methodological credibility.

scalable.rationale: Studies benchmark-scale problems; cell-scale stress tests not part of the comparison.

how_to_validate.rationale: FAIR comparison framework itself is a borrowable validation methodology for surrogate selection.

candidates.paper_title: Learning two-phase microstructure evolution using neural operators and autoencoder architectures

useful_outcomes.rationale: Autoencoder + DeepONet replaces phase-field solver for microstructure evolution — direct surrogate-emulation example.

immediate_benefit.rationale: Latent-space + operator pipeline is reusable, but training data generation from full solver still needed.

plausible.rationale: npj Comp Mat paper with explicit interpolation and extrapolation accelerations over phase-field solver.

scalable.rationale: Latent-space compression makes higher-resolution microstructures tractable; cell-scale untested.

how_to_validate.rationale: Validates against high-fidelity phase-field simulations on both interpolation and extrapolation tasks.

candidates.paper_title: Variational Physics-informed Neural Operator (VINO) for solving partial differential equations
candidates.paper_journal: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering

useful_outcomes.rationale: VINO trains label-free using variational PDE energy and outperforms baselines as mesh resolution grows.

immediate_benefit.rationale: Variational formulation needs domain discretisation infrastructure that biology teams may lack.

plausible.rationale: CMAME paper with comparative results showing VINO superiority at fine meshes.

scalable.rationale: Performance improves with mesh resolution, indicating scalability potential for spatial submodels.

how_to_validate.rationale: Mesh-refinement studies and comparison to existing operators provide an adoptable ablation pattern.

candidates.paper_title: Deep transfer operator learning for partial differential equations under conditional shift

useful_outcomes.rationale: DeepONet transfer learning under conditional shift makes surrogates reusable across related PDE tasks — supports emulation in scarce-data biology.

immediate_benefit.rationale: Transfer recipe with hybrid loss is implementable but RKHS embeddings add nontrivial code.

plausible.rationale: Nature Machine Intelligence paper grounded in conditional-embedding operator theory with multiple PDE demos.

scalable.rationale: Transfer reduces data needs but the underlying DeepONet scale matches, not exceeds, the original.

how_to_validate.rationale: Diverse transfer-learning scenarios with quantitative comparisons constitute a borrowable validation suite.
